meta.title: Snakes & Ladders
meta.subtitle: Scale from local SQLite to 99.999% global databases — solve schema, HA, caching & query checks.

1.title: Local SQLite & Port 5432 Prototype
1.quip: "One local .db file on a laptop—zero connection pools, zero replicas, and big global ambitions."
1.tip: Choose the right database model early: relational (Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner), document (Firestore), wide-column (Bigtable), or in-memory (Memorystore).

100.title: Zero-Downtime Global Database Fleet!
100.quip: "Sub-5ms p99 reads worldwide, zero lock contention, continuous PITR, and five-nines external consistency."
100.tip: World-class database reliability combines multi-region active-active or synchronous HA, connection pooling, hot-key prevention, and practiced PITR drills.

ladders.title: Cloud Spanner Multi-Region (99.999%)
ladders.quip: "Active-active relational consistency across continents with zero failover downtime."
ladders.tip: Cloud Spanner uses TrueTime to deliver externally consistent distributed ACID transactions with a 99.999% multi-region SLA.
ladders.q: How does Cloud Spanner achieve external consistency across continents without global lock bottlenecks?
opts: Hardware-assisted TrueTime atomic/GPS clocks bound clock uncertainty across data centers for lock-free snapshot reads and serializable writes
Asynchronous eventual consistency that reconciles conflicts once a week
Routing all reads and writes through a single VM in one zone
ladders.why: TrueTime bounds clock drift explicitly so Spanner can order transactions globally and serve consistent reads without locking.

ladders.title: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL Columnar Engine
ladders.quip: "100% PostgreSQL compatible, 4x faster transactional throughput, and up to 100x faster analytical queries!"
ladders.tip: AlloyDB separates compute from storage and accelerates real-time BI queries on operational data via its adaptive in-memory columnar engine.
ladders.q: How does AlloyDB handle storage replication and read-pool scaling compared to standard PostgreSQL?
opts: Storage is disaggregated across a regional intelligent storage layer, so adding Read Pool nodes does not require copying full disk volumes
Every read replica must copy the entire 10 TB disk over the internet first
AlloyDB only stores data in browser cookies
ladders.why: AlloyDB's disaggregated regional storage writes once across zones while compute and read pools attach to the shared storage layer quickly.

ladders.title: AlloyDB AI & ScaNN Vector Index
ladders.quip: "Ran millisecond hybrid SQL + semantic vector search using the `alloydb_scann` index right inside PostgreSQL!"
ladders.tip: Use AlloyDB AI (`alloydb_scann` index + `google_ml_integration`) to combine relational filters with high-speed vector similarity search.
ladders.q: Which specialized index in AlloyDB AI accelerates high-dimensional vector similarity search over standard pgvector HNSW/IVFFlat?
opts: The `alloydb_scann` index powered by Google Research's ScaNN algorithm
A B-tree index on raw 8 KB text strings
An unindexed `LIKE '%query%'` full table scan
ladders.why: The `alloydb_scann` index delivers significantly higher QPS and lower memory footprint for vector similarity search.

ladders.title: Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus Data Cache
ladders.quip: "Planned maintenance completed in under a second and local NVMe SSD Data Cache cut read latency by 75%."
ladders.tip: Choose Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus for 99.99% availability SLA, near-zero downtime maintenance, and local SSD Data Cache.
ladders.q: What key capabilities does Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus add over the standard Cloud SQL Enterprise edition?
opts: 99.99% availability SLA, sub-second planned maintenance downtime, local SSD Data Cache, and 35-day log retention
Removes the need for primary keys on tables
Only supports read-only CSV files
ladders.why: Enterprise Plus is engineered for tier-1 relational workloads requiring high performance and minimal maintenance disruption.

ladders.title: Cloud SQL Auth Proxy + IAM Auth
ladders.quip: "Zero static DB passwords and zero CIDR allowlists—every connection uses TLS 1.3 and short-lived IAM tokens!"
ladders.tip: Use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy (or language connectors) with automatic IAM database authentication.
ladders.docLabel: About the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy
ladders.q: What two security problems does the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy solve automatically?
opts: Encrypts traffic with mutually verified TLS certificates and authenticates via IAM without managing static IP allowlists
Replaces SQL queries with GraphQL automatically
Compresses images stored in Cloud Storage
ladders.why: The Auth Proxy handles ephemeral certificate validation and IAM token refresh transparently.

ladders.title: Cloud Bigtable Wide-Column Scale
ladders.quip: "Scaled from 3 nodes to 30 nodes during peak trading and sustained 5 million ops/sec at 4ms p99 latency."
ladders.tip: Use Cloud Bigtable for high-throughput, low-latency key-value and time-series workloads at terabyte-to-petabyte scale.
ladders.q: How does Cloud Bigtable scale throughput when you add nodes to a cluster?
opts: Throughput scales linearly because compute nodes are separated from Colossus distributed storage and rebalance tablet pointers in metadata
Every new node must copy 100% of the disk over SSH before serving
Adding nodes decreases write throughput
ladders.why: Bigtable tablets store data in Colossus; nodes hold metadata pointers and in-memory memtables, allowing rapid rebalancing.

ladders.title: Bigtable Data Boost (Serverless Batch)
ladders.quip: "Ran a heavy Spark & BigQuery federated scan over production Bigtable using serverless Data Boost—zero impact on live user p99 latency!"
ladders.tip: Use Bigtable Data Boost to run batch reads, Spark jobs, or BigQuery federated queries on isolated serverless compute.
ladders.q: Why use Bigtable Data Boost when running large analytical batch jobs against a production Bigtable instance?
opts: Executes batch reads on isolated, pay-per-use serverless compute so production serving nodes and latency are completely unaffected
Deletes old rows to make queries faster
Converts Bigtable into a single-node SQLite file
ladders.why: Data Boost reads underlying storage via separate serverless compute, isolating real-time app traffic from batch analytics.

ladders.title: Firestore Multi-Region (`nam5` / `eur3`)
ladders.quip: "Synced millions of mobile clients in real time with offline caching and 99.999% multi-region strong consistency."
ladders.tip: Use Firestore for serverless document storage with real-time client listeners, ACID transactions, and automatic indexing.
ladders.q: How does Firestore guarantee fast query performance regardless of how many million documents are in a collection?
opts: Every query is backed by an index, so query latency scales with the size of the *result set*, not the total collection size
It scans every document in the database on every query
It limits collections to 100 documents max
ladders.why: Firestore's index-backed architecture ensures query time depends only on the number of results returned.

ladders.title: Memorystore for Valkey / Redis Cluster
ladders.quip: "Sub-millisecond cache hits absorbed 92% of product catalog reads—primary database CPU barely broke a sweat."
ladders.tip: Place Memorystore in front of relational or document databases to absorb hot reads and session state at sub-millisecond latency.
ladders.q: In a Cache-Aside pattern with Memorystore and Cloud SQL, what happens on a cache miss?
opts: The application reads the record from Cloud SQL, writes it into Memorystore with a TTL, and returns it to the caller
The application returns an HTTP 500 error immediately
Memorystore deletes the Cloud SQL table
ladders.why: Cache-aside populates the cache on demand with a TTL so subsequent requests hit sub-millisecond memory.

ladders.title: Database Migration Service (DMS) + Gemini
ladders.quip: "Converted legacy Oracle PL/SQL stored procedures to AlloyDB PostgreSQL with Gemini-assisted conversion and continuous CDC cutover!"
ladders.tip: Use Database Migration Service (DMS) for serverless, continuous CDC database migrations with minimal cutover downtime.
ladders.q: How does Database Migration Service (DMS) minimize downtime when migrating a live production database to Cloud SQL or AlloyDB?
opts: Performs an initial full dump followed by continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) replication until you promote the target during a brief cutover
Requires shutting down the source database for 2 weeks while copying files
Only migrates table names without row data
ladders.why: Continuous CDC keeps the target database in near-real-time sync so final cutover takes minutes rather than hours.

ladders.title: Datastream Real-Time CDC to BigQuery
ladders.quip: "Operational PostgreSQL inserts and updates land in BigQuery for analytics within seconds—zero custom ETL cron jobs."
ladders.tip: Use Datastream for serverless Change Data Capture (CDC) streaming from MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, or SQL Server into BigQuery.
ladders.q: Why use Datastream to replicate operational database changes to BigQuery instead of running heavy analytical `SELECT` queries on the primary OLTP database?
opts: Reads from the database's replication log (WAL/binlog) with minimal OLTP overhead and streams changes continuously into BigQuery
Locks all operational tables for 4 hours every afternoon
Deletes rows from the source database after reading them
ladders.why: Log-based CDC captures changes non-intrusively and offloads heavy analytical queries to BigQuery.

ladders.title: Spanner Graph (ISO GQL + SQL)
ladders.quip: "Traversed 4-hop payment relationships with ISO GQL graph patterns inside the same ACID transaction as relational tables!"
ladders.tip: Use Spanner Graph to query property graphs using ISO GQL alongside standard SQL without moving data to a separate graph silo.
ladders.q: What architectural problem does Spanner Graph eliminate?
opts: Eliminates maintaining a separate graph database and brittle ETL sync pipelines—graph GQL and relational SQL query the same live tables
Replaces CSS styling in web apps
Eliminates the need for primary keys
ladders.why: Unified relational and graph storage keeps graph traversals strongly consistent with operational transactions.

ladders.title: Spanner Change Streams
ladders.quip: "Every Spanner mutation streamed cleanly through Dataflow to downstream search indexes and audit sinks in real time."
ladders.tip: Use Spanner Change Streams to watch and stream data modifications (inserts, updates, deletes) across your database.
ladders.q: How can downstream services react to row mutations in Cloud Spanner without polling tables?
opts: Enable Spanner Change Streams and process the change records via Dataflow or Kafka/Pub/Sub connectors
Run `SELECT *` every 100ms from a cron script
Parse raw disk image snapshots manually
ladders.why: Change Streams capture every committed mutation in commit-timestamp order with high scalability.

ladders.title: Spanner Geo-Partitioning
ladders.quip: "One global Spanner table—EU users' rows live and serve in Europe while US users' rows live in the US!"
ladders.tip: Use Spanner Geo-Partitioning (placement keys) to pin specific row partitions to regional placements for low latency and residency.
ladders.q: What does Cloud Spanner Geo-Partitioning allow you to do within a single database table?
opts: Pin specific subsets of rows to designated regional placements based on a placement key while maintaining a single unified global schema
Split every column into a different cloud provider
Disable ACID transactions on international rows
ladders.why: Geo-partitioning delivers local read/write latency and data residency compliance without sharding into separate databases.

ladders.title: Spanner Interleaved Tables (`INTERLEAVE IN PARENT`)
ladders.quip: "Co-located `OrderItems` physically inside their parent `Orders` split—parent-child joins completed in a single local read!"
ladders.tip: Use `INTERLEAVE IN PARENT` in Cloud Spanner for strong parent-child locality so joins avoid cross-machine network hops.
ladders.q: When should you declare a child table with `INTERLEAVE IN PARENT` in Cloud Spanner?
opts: When child rows (e.g., `OrderLines`) are frequently queried and joined together with their parent row (`Order`) by shared primary key prefix
When the two tables have no relationship or shared keys
When storing static CSS files
ladders.why: Interleaving physically co-locates child rows with their parent row on the same storage split, making parent-child joins ultra-fast.

ladders.title: Cloud SQL & AlloyDB Read Replicas
ladders.quip: "Offloaded heavy analytics & reporting traffic to Read Replicas—primary writer latency stayed flat at 2ms."
ladders.tip: Route read-heavy reporting queries to Read Replicas (or AlloyDB Read Pools) and configure cross-region replicas for DR.
ladders.q: Which two purposes do Cross-Region Read Replicas serve in Cloud SQL and AlloyDB?
opts: Serving low-latency read traffic closer to users in other regions AND acting as a promotable disaster-recovery target if the primary region fails
Doubling primary write throughput in the home region
Automatically encrypting client browsers
ladders.why: Cross-region replicas provide both geo-distributed read scaling and regional disaster recovery promotion.

ladders.title: Firebase Data Connect (Cloud SQL)
ladders.quip: "Defined our schema once—got relational Cloud SQL PostgreSQL plus auto-generated type-safe web & mobile SDKs!"
ladders.tip: Use Firebase Data Connect to pair managed Cloud SQL PostgreSQL with generated type-safe client SDKs and vector search.
ladders.q: How does Firebase Data Connect secure client queries against a Cloud SQL PostgreSQL backend?
opts: Compiles predefined application queries/mutations into server-enforced PostgreSQL prepared statements gated by declarative `@auth` directives
Lets browsers send raw arbitrary `DROP TABLE` SQL strings over the internet
Stores the entire PostgreSQL database in localStorage
ladders.why: Clients can only invoke pre-declared, auth-checked operations—never arbitrary raw SQL from the browser.

ladders.title: BigQuery Federated Queries (`EXTERNAL_QUERY`)
ladders.quip: "Joined live operational lookup tables in AlloyDB/Spanner directly with historical petabytes in BigQuery in one SQL statement!"
ladders.tip: Use BigQuery `EXTERNAL_QUERY` federated connections to join live Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, or Spanner data with BigQuery tables.
ladders.q: How do you reduce data transfer overhead when using `EXTERNAL_QUERY` to query Cloud SQL or Spanner from BigQuery?
opts: Push predicates (`WHERE` filters) and column projections inside the inner `EXTERNAL_QUERY` SQL string so the operational DB returns only needed rows
Pull the entire 5 TB operational table into BigQuery before filtering
Run the query 100 times in a loop
ladders.why: Filtering and aggregating inside the federated query string minimizes rows transferred from the operational database.

snakes.title: Monotonic Auto-Increment Primary Key in Spanner
snakes.quip: "Used `1, 2, 3, 4...` as the primary key in Cloud Spanner—100% of writes hammered a single split on one server!"
snakes.tip: Never use monotonically increasing integers or timestamps as the leading key column in Spanner; use UUIDv4 or bit-reversed sequences.
snakes.prevent: Use UUIDv4, `BIT_REVERSED_POSITIVE` sequences, or shard-hash prefixes for primary keys.
snakes.detect: Spanner Key Visualizer showing a bright red line along the bottom/top edge of the key space.
snakes.recover: Migrate to a bit-reversed sequence or composite hash-prefixed key to spread writes across splits.
snakes.q: Why does a monotonically increasing timestamp or integer primary key cause a write hotspot in Cloud Spanner?
opts: Spanner range-partitions rows in key order, so every new sequential key lands on the exact same last split on a single server
Spanner only supports string keys under 4 characters
Sequential numbers break SQL syntax
snakes.why: Distributing leading key values (via UUIDv4 or bit-reversal) spreads inserts evenly across all splits.

snakes.title: Sequential Timestamp Row Keys in Bigtable
snakes.quip: "Named every Bigtable row key `20261112_163000_deviceId`—one tablet node hit 100% CPU while the other 19 nodes sat idle!"
snakes.tip: Put high-cardinality attributes (e.g., hashed `deviceId` or `tenantId`) first in Bigtable row keys, followed by reverse/bucketed timestamps.
snakes.prevent: Design row keys with a high-cardinality prefix (`user_hash#reverse_timestamp`) and test with Key Visualizer.
snakes.detect: Bigtable Key Visualizer showing a single hot horizontal row-key band and `hot_tablets` monitoring alerts.
snakes.recover: Redesign the row-key prefix to distribute writes across tablet ranges and dual-write/backfill.
snakes.q: How should you order `sensor_id` and `timestamp` in a Cloud Bigtable row key when querying recent readings per sensor?
opts: `sensor_id#reverse_timestamp` so writes spread across sensors and recent readings for a sensor sit contiguously at the top
`timestamp#sensor_id` so all sensors write to the exact same tablet simultaneously
Store the entire year of readings in a single cell
snakes.why: Leading with `sensor_id` distributes writes across tablets while `reverse_timestamp` makes 'latest N readings for sensor X' a fast range scan.

snakes.title: Serverless Spike Exhausted Postgres `max_connections`
snakes.quip: "Cloud Run scaled to 600 instances during a traffic surge; each opened 5 DB connections and hit `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved`!"
snakes.tip: Pool connections (PgBouncer / Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus / AlloyDB connection pooling), reuse pools globally, and cap `--max-instances`.
snakes.prevent: Enable connection pooling, initialize pools in global scope, tune `--concurrency`, and bound `--max-instances`.
snakes.recover: Cap `--max-instances` on serverless callers and enable managed connection pooling / PgBouncer.
snakes.q: What is the most effective architectural fix when hundreds of serverless instances exhaust PostgreSQL `max_connections`?
opts: Use connection pooling (e.g., PgBouncer / built-in pooling), reuse pools in global scope, and bound serverless `--max-instances`
Set `max_connections = 500000` on a 1-vCPU database
Create a new database instance for every HTTP request
snakes.why: Each raw PostgreSQL backend process consumes memory and IPC overhead; connection pooling multiplexes thousands of app clients over a small pool of server connections.

snakes.title: Public `0.0.0.0/0` Authorized Network on Cloud SQL
snakes.quip: "Whitelisted `0.0.0.0/0` on Cloud SQL to test from a coffee shop—internet password-spraying bots arrived in 30 seconds!"
snakes.tip: Enforce `sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks` via Org Policy and connect strictly via Private IP / PSC and the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.
snakes.prevent: Enforce Org Policy `constraints/sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks` and disable public IPs on production databases.
snakes.detect: Security Command Center `SQL_WORLD_READABLE` / `OPEN_FIREWALL` findings & Database Center security alerts.
snakes.recover: Clear `0.0.0.0/0` from Authorized Networks immediately, rotate credentials, and switch to Cloud SQL Auth Proxy over Private IP.
snakes.docLabel: Configure Private IP for Cloud SQL
snakes.q: Which Organization Policy constraint blocks anyone from adding public Authorized Networks to Cloud SQL instances?
opts: `constraints/sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks` (paired with Private IP / Cloud SQL Auth Proxy)
`constraints/storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess`
`constraints/compute.disableSerialPortAccess`
snakes.why: Enforcing `sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks` prevents broad IP allowlisting on Cloud SQL.

snakes.title: Single-Zone Prod Database Hit by Zonal Outage
snakes.quip: "Deployed production Cloud SQL in Zonal mode (`--availability-type=ZONAL`)—when the zone had an issue, checkout went dark with no standby!"
snakes.tip: Always enable Regional High Availability (`--availability-type=REGIONAL`) on production Cloud SQL and AlloyDB instances.
snakes.prevent: Deploy production instances with `--availability-type=REGIONAL` (synchronous primary + standby across two zones).
snakes.detect: Database Center availability posture warning flagging single-zone production instances.
snakes.recover: Update the instance to `--availability-type=REGIONAL` so a synchronous standby is provisioned in a secondary zone.
snakes.q: How is data replicated between the primary and standby instance in a Regional High Availability (HA) Cloud SQL configuration?
opts: Synchronously at the regional persistent storage layer across two zones in the same region
By emailing CSV exports once every midnight
Via browser localStorage
snakes.why: Synchronous regional storage replication guarantees zero data loss (RPO = 0) on automatic zonal failover.

snakes.title: Used Read-Write Transaction for Read-Only Spanner Reporting
snakes.quip: "Ran a slow dashboard query inside a Read-Write transaction in Spanner—held shared locks across 50,000 rows and stalled live orders!"
snakes.tip: Use lock-free Read-Only transactions (`snapshot`) or bounded staleness reads for all non-mutating queries in Cloud Spanner.
snakes.prevent: Use Read-Only transactions (`snapshot`) for all reporting, search, and lookup queries that do not write.
snakes.detect: Spanner `LOCK_STATS` system tables showing high lock wait times on read-heavy tables.
snakes.recover: Switch the reporting code from a Read-Write transaction to a lock-free Read-Only snapshot.
snakes.q: Why should read-only queries in Cloud Spanner never use a Read-Write transaction context?
opts: Read-Write transactions acquire shared read locks that block concurrent writers, whereas Read-Only transactions read lock-free via TrueTime MVCC
Read-Write transactions cannot execute `SELECT` statements
Read-Only transactions delete rows after reading
snakes.why: Spanner's multi-version concurrency control lets Read-Only transactions execute at a timestamp with zero locking.

snakes.title: Accidental `DELETE FROM orders` Without Point-in-Time Recovery
snakes.quip: "A migration script wiped the `orders` table at 3 PM—and because PITR was off, the only backup was from 15 hours earlier!"
snakes.tip: Enable Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) on Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, and Firestore to restore to any second.
snakes.prevent: Enable Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) and automated backups on all production databases.
snakes.detect: Database Center data-protection posture checks flagging instances with PITR disabled.
snakes.recover: Enable PITR immediately; during an incident, clone/restore to the exact timestamp just prior to the bad mutation.
snakes.q: What recovery capability does Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) provide beyond daily automated snapshots?
opts: Continuous transaction log (WAL/binlog) archival allowing you to restore a database clone to any specific second within the retention window
Automatic translation of SQL into Python
Free unlimited compute CPU
snakes.why: Replaying write-ahead logs on top of a base backup recovers data up to the exact second before human error struck.

snakes.title: Single-Document Global Counter Contention in Firestore
snakes.quip: "Incremented a single `metrics/live_users` Firestore document on every login—hit document write contention limits and threw `ABORTED`!"
snakes.tip: Shard high-frequency counters across N distributed counter documents in Firestore or track ephemeral counts in Memorystore.
snakes.prevent: Use Sharded Distributed Counters in Firestore or increment high-velocity counters in Memorystore.
snakes.detect: Firestore `ABORTED` transaction contention errors and Key Visualizer single-document write spikes.
snakes.recover: Split the single counter document into `shards/0..N` subdocuments or offload real-time counters to Memorystore.
snakes.q: Why does updating the exact same Firestore document 500 times per second from concurrent clients cause contention errors?
opts: Each document update must serialize ACID index and storage commits for that document key—sharding across N documents distributes the writes
Firestore only allows 1 write per hour across the entire project
JSON documents cannot store integers
snakes.why: Distributed counters spread concurrent increments across multiple documents and sum them on read.

snakes.title: Missing Index on 100M-Row Table Pinned DB CPU at 100%
snakes.quip: "Added a new `WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND region = 'APAC'` query on a 100-million-row table without a composite index—every poll scanned the whole table!"
snakes.tip: Use Cloud SQL / AlloyDB Query Insights and Index Advisor to identify slow full-table scans and create covering composite indexes.
snakes.prevent: Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` in staging and review Index Advisor recommendations in Query Insights.
snakes.detect: Query Insights showing high `shared_blks_read` / sequential scan latency and 100% CPU utilization.
snakes.recover: Create the composite index concurrently (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`) so live writes are not blocked.
snakes.q: In PostgreSQL on Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, how do you build a new index on a live production table without locking concurrent writes?
opts: Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`
Shut down the application for 3 hours while running `DROP TABLE`
Restart the database every 10 seconds
snakes.why: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` builds the index without acquiring locks that block concurrent inserts, updates, or deletes.

snakes.title: Created New DB Connection Pool Inside Every HTTP Request
snakes.quip: "Called `sqlalchemy.create_engine()` inside the Flask route function instead of module scope—leaked 200 connection pools in 30 seconds!"
snakes.tip: Always instantiate database connection pools once in global/module scope so warm container instances reuse connections.
snakes.prevent: Initialize the connection pool in global scope outside the request handler and set `pool_size` / `max_overflow` limits.
snakes.detect: Database connection count climbing linearly with each HTTP request until connections are refused.
snakes.recover: Move `create_engine()` / pool initialization to global module scope and deploy the fix.
snakes.q: Why must a database connection pool be declared in global/module scope in Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions?
opts: So a warm container instance reuses the same pool across thousands of requests instead of leaking a new pool on every request
Global variables are encrypted in RAM
Local variables cannot store strings
snakes.why: Per-request pool creation defeats connection pooling completely and rapidly exhausts database sockets.

snakes.title: Cache Stampede When Hot Homepage Key Expired at Midnight
snakes.quip: "The cached homepage payload expired at `00:00:00`—8,000 concurrent requests all missed Memorystore at the same millisecond and stampeded the DB!"
snakes.tip: Use request coalescing (singleflight / mutex lock), jittered TTLs, or proactive background refresh for hot cache keys.
snakes.prevent: Add random jitter to cache TTLs and use singleflight / lock coalescing so only 1 worker recomputes an expired hot key.
snakes.detect: Periodic spikes in Memorystore cache-miss rate coinciding with sudden 100% DB CPU spikes.
snakes.recover: Warm the hot cache keys proactively and deploy singleflight request coalescing with jittered TTLs.
snakes.q: How do you prevent a 'cache stampede' (thundering herd) when a popular Memorystore key's TTL expires under heavy traffic?
opts: Use singleflight/mutex request coalescing (so only one worker queries the DB to repopulate the cache) and add random jitter to key TTLs
Disable caching completely
Set all cache TTLs to 1 millisecond
snakes.why: Coalescing concurrent cache misses into a single database lookup protects the database when a hot key expires.

snakes.title: Abandoned `idle in transaction` Session Blocked Postgres `AUTOVACUUM`
snakes.quip: "A developer's laptop left an uncommitted `BEGIN;` transaction open over the weekend—blocked `autovacuum` dead-tuple cleanup and spiked table bloat + XID age!"
snakes.tip: Set `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` in PostgreSQL flags and monitor transaction ID (`XID`) age in Cloud Monitoring.
snakes.detect: Cloud Monitoring alert on `database/postgresql/transaction_id_utilization` and bloated dead-tuple counts.
snakes.recover: Terminate the stuck session (`pg_terminate_backend`), let `VACUUM` reclaim dead tuples, and set `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`.
snakes.q: Which PostgreSQL database flag automatically terminates abandoned client sessions that sit `idle in transaction` holding snapshots open?
opts: `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`
`max_connections`
`work_mem`
snakes.why: Automatically closing abandoned `idle in transaction` sessions prevents them from blocking `autovacuum` and causing transaction ID wraparound.

snakes.title: Cross-Region N+1 Chatty SQL Loop
snakes.quip: "Fetched 100 orders and then ran `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?` 100 times in a `for` loop across regions—8 seconds of pure network RTT!"
snakes.tip: Replace N+1 query loops with a single `JOIN` or `WHERE id = ANY($1)` batch query, and co-locate compute in the database's region.
snakes.prevent: Batch lookups using `JOIN` or `ANY($1)` and deploy compute in the same region as the database (or local read replica).
snakes.detect: Cloud Trace waterfall showing 100+ sequential short SQL spans per HTTP request.
snakes.recover: Refactor the N+1 loop into a single batched SQL query and co-locate compute and database regions.
snakes.q: Why does executing 100 sequential 1ms SQL queries from `us-east1` against a database in `europe-west1` take over 7 seconds?
opts: Each sequential query pays ~75ms of transatlantic network round-trip latency (`100 × 75ms = 7.5s`); batch into 1 query and co-locate regions
PostgreSQL pauses for 75ms after every semicolon
Fiber-optic cables only transmit 1 query per second
snakes.why: Eliminating N+1 round-trips and co-locating compute with data reduces 100 network hops to 1 local hop.

snakes.title: Un-Interleaved Parent-Child Tables in Spanner
snakes.quip: "Stored `Invoices` and `InvoiceLines` as top-level independent tables in Spanner—every invoice lookup required cross-machine distributed joins!"
snakes.tip: Declare child tables with `INTERLEAVE IN PARENT` in Cloud Spanner when they are predominantly accessed by parent primary key.
snakes.prevent: Design hierarchical entities with composite keys `(parent_id, child_id)` and `INTERLEAVE IN PARENT`.
snakes.detect: Spanner Query Execution Plans showing high cross-split distributed join latency on parent-child queries.
snakes.recover: Migrate the child table to an interleaved schema (`INTERLEAVE IN PARENT`) so child rows co-locate with their parent.
snakes.q: What is the performance drawback of keeping tightly coupled parent and child tables non-interleaved in Cloud Spanner?
opts: Parent and child rows are stored in separate splits potentially on different servers, requiring network RPCs during joins
Spanner blocks `JOIN` syntax on non-interleaved tables
Non-interleaved tables cannot have indexes
snakes.why: Interleaving physically co-locates parent and child rows on the same split, turning joins into fast local reads.

snakes.title: Unbounded Firestore Collection Listener Without `.limit()`
snakes.quip: "Attached an unfiltered `onSnapshot(collection(db, 'messages'))` listener in the web app—every user opening the page downloaded all 80,000 historical messages!"
snakes.tip: Always bound Firestore queries and real-time listeners with `.orderBy(...).limit(N)` and cursor pagination (`startAfter`).
snakes.prevent: Enforce `.limit(N)` on all client queries and validate `request.query.limit <= 100` inside Firestore Security Rules!
snakes.detect: Cloud Monitoring `firestore.googleapis.com/document/read_count` spiking disproportionately to active users.
snakes.recover: Deploy `.limit(50)` with `startAfter` pagination in the client AND enforce `request.query.limit` in `firestore.rules`.
snakes.q: How can you enforce at the server level that a client cannot run an unbounded collection read in Firestore?
opts: Check `request.query.limit <= 100` inside your `firestore.rules` security rules alongside `.limit()` in the client query
Hope users never scroll down
Rename the collection every hour
snakes.why: Enforcing `request.query.limit` in Firestore Security Rules guarantees even a modified client cannot request thousands of documents at once.

snakes.title: Revoked DB Service Agent Access to CMEK Encryption Key
snakes.quip: "An IAM cleanup script removed the Cloud SQL Service Agent from the Cloud KMS CMEK key—the database immediately lost access to its encrypted disks!"
snakes.tip: Protect Google Service Agent `cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` bindings on CMEK keys and configure KMS key revocation action policies.
snakes.prevent: Protect `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@...` Service Agent bindings on CMEK keys using IAM Deny exclusions.
snakes.detect: Cloud Audit Logs KMS `PERMISSION_DENIED` alerts and Database Center CMEK health warnings.
snakes.recover: Restore `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for the database Service Agent on the KMS key and restart/recover the instance.
snakes.q: What happens if the Cloud SQL or Spanner Service Agent loses `cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` permission on its active Cloud KMS CMEK key?
opts: The database service can no longer decrypt its storage keys, rendering the instance inaccessible until KMS permissions are restored
The database automatically switches to plaintext
Nothing happens until the year 2099
snakes.why: CMEK gives you ultimate cryptographic control—revoking the service agent's KMS access cuts off data decryption immediately.

snakes.title: Unencrypted Database Connections Without `requireSsl`
snakes.quip: "Connected to the database over a hybrid network without SSL/TLS enforcement—credentials and customer rows traveled in cleartext over the wire!"
snakes.tip: Enforce SSL/TLS (`requireSsl` / `ENCRYPTED_ONLY`) on all Cloud SQL and AlloyDB instances, or use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.
snakes.prevent: Enforce Org Policy `sql.Concat` / `ENCRYPTED_ONLY` SSL mode and connect via Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.
snakes.detect: Security Command Center `SQL_UNENCRYPTED_CONNECTIONS` finding & Database Center posture checks.
snakes.recover: Enable `ENCRYPTED_ONLY` SSL mode on the database and route clients through the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.
snakes.q: How do you guarantee that a Cloud SQL instance rejects any client attempting to connect without TLS encryption?
opts: Set the instance SSL mode to `ENCRYPTED_ONLY` (or `TRUSTED_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED`) and use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy
Use port 80 instead of port 5432
Add `ssl=false` to the connection string
snakes.why: Enforcing `ENCRYPTED_ONLY` on the server ensures unencrypted connection handshakes are rejected immediately.

snakes.title: Stored 50 MB PDF Blobs Inside Bigtable Cells
snakes.quip: "Tried to stuff raw 50 MB PDF files directly into Cloud Bigtable cells—blew past the 10 MB cell limit and choked tablet compactions!"
snakes.tip: Keep Cloud Bigtable cell values small (< 100 KB ideal, 10 MB hard limit); store large blobs in Cloud Storage and keep only the `gs://` URI in Bigtable.
snakes.prevent: Store binary blobs/files in Cloud Storage and store only metadata and the `gs://` object URI in Bigtable.
snakes.detect: Bigtable client `InvalidArgument` / oversized mutation errors and high tablet compaction latency.
snakes.recover: Offload large payloads to Cloud Storage buckets and replace the cell contents with `gs://` URI references.
snakes.q: How should you store 50 MB media or PDF files that need to be looked up via a Cloud Bigtable index?
opts: Store the 50 MB file in Cloud Storage and store its `gs://` URI and metadata in the Bigtable row
Base64-encode the 50 MB file into a single Bigtable cell
Split the PDF across 50,000 column family names
snakes.why: Bigtable is optimized for small cells (<100 KB); pairing Cloud Storage for blobs with Bigtable for fast metadata lookup gives the best of both worlds.

shields.title: Google Cloud Database Center
shields.quip: "Unified fleet health, HA posture, backup verification, and security recommendations across every DB in one console."
shields.tip: Use Database Center to continuously audit HA, PITR backups, encryption, and performance across Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, and Bigtable.

shields.title: Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)
shields.quip: "Continuous write-ahead log archival armed—ready to clone or rewind to any second within the retention window."
shields.tip: Enable Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) on Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, and Firestore to recover from accidental deletes.

shields.title: IAM Database Authentication
shields.quip: "Short-lived OAuth2 IAM tokens replaced static database passwords across every microservice."
shields.tip: Enable IAM database authentication on Cloud SQL and AlloyDB to eliminate password rotation toil.

shields.title: Spanner & Bigtable Key Visualizer
shields.quip: "Spotted an asymmetric read/write hotspot on a key prefix before it ever breached our latency SLO!"
shields.tip: Inspect Key Visualizer heatmaps regularly on Spanner, Bigtable, and Firestore to catch hotspotting early.

shields.title: Query Insights & Index Advisor
shields.quip: "Pinpointed the exact microservice tag and SQL statement causing lock waits in 15 seconds."
shields.tip: Use Query Insights and Index Advisor on Cloud SQL and AlloyDB to trace slow queries with OpenTelemetry tags.

shields.title: Managed Connection Pooling / PgBouncer
shields.quip: "Multiplexed 2,000 serverless client connections smoothly over 50 warm PostgreSQL backend processes."
shields.tip: Use connection pooling to protect relational databases from serverless connection spikes.

shields.title: Cloud Spanner Managed Autoscaler
shields.quip: "Spanner scaled processing units up ahead of high-priority CPU thresholds and scaled back down overnight."
shields.tip: Enable Managed Autoscaler on Cloud Spanner to keep high-priority CPU utilization within target bounds automatically.

shields.title: Database Deletion Protection Flag
shields.quip: "Blocked an accidental `terraform destroy` from wiping the production database instance!"
shields.tip: Enable `--deletion-protection` on all production Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, and Bigtable instances.

shields.title: Private Service Connect DB Endpoints
shields.quip: "Connected app VPCs privately to AlloyDB and Cloud SQL without VPC peering or overlapping CIDR issues."
shields.tip: Use Private Service Connect (PSC) endpoints to connect to Cloud SQL and AlloyDB privately across VPCs.

shields.title: Firestore Security Rules + Emulator Suite
shields.quip: "CI unit tests verified every path, ownership check, and `request.query.limit` constraint before deploy."
shields.tip: Test Firestore Security Rules against the local Emulator Suite in CI and enforce query limits and schema types.

shields.title: Bigtable Multi-Cluster App Profiles
shields.quip: "Multi-cluster routing automatically failed over live reads and writes when a zone had maintenance."
shields.tip: Use Multi-Cluster Routing in Bigtable App Profiles for automatic high-availability failover across clusters.

shields.title: Memorystore Multi-Zone High Availability
shields.quip: "Cross-zone replica promoted in seconds with zero cache cold-start during zonal maintenance."
shields.tip: Deploy Memorystore with multi-zone read replicas / cluster HA to keep cache hit rates high during zone events.

shields.title: Backup and DR Locked Immutable Vault
shields.quip: "Enforced retention locks on database backups—immutable even if project admin credentials are compromised."
shields.tip: Store critical database backups in Backup and DR Service with locked minimum retention periods.

shields.title: Spanner & Bigtable Row TTL Policies
shields.quip: "Expired session and audit rows purged automatically in the background at low priority—zero manual delete spikes!"
shields.tip: Use built-in Row Time-to-Live (TTL) policies in Spanner, Firestore, and Bigtable to expire stale data automatically.

shields.title: Org Policy `sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks`
shields.quip: "Prevented public IP allowlists on every Cloud SQL instance across the entire organization folder tree."

shields.title: Cloud KMS Autokey CMEK for Databases
shields.quip: "Automated per-database CMEK key provisioning with separation of duties and scheduled rotation."
shields.tip: Use Cloud KMS Autokey to provision compliant Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for every database.
